file-description.file-description-heading: This file contains thermal insulation and material data for the Thermal Calculator application.
file-description-text: - Contains thermal conductivity values for various insulation materials
- Lists R-values for different material thicknesses
- Includes notes and warnings for correct application

log-changes: Integrated all missing specific insulation products (PIR, Phenolic, XPS, EPS variants).
Added alternative generic insulation values (Mineral Wool, Glass Wool, XPS, EPS, Wood Fibre, Urea Formaldehyde, Wood Wool Slab).

Expanded Masonry-Materials with specific brick densities/conditions, concrete block types (Forterra, Gryphonn), AAC variants, additional stone types (Malta BCA Granite), and alternative mortar values.

Expanded Concrete-And-Screeds with various concrete types/densities (Heavy Weight, No-Fines, Aerated Generic, Low Thermal Conductivity, Precast Hollow Core material) and screed variants (CIBSE cement-sand, Agilia Anhydrite).
Added alternative values for Roofing-Materials-Outer-Coverings (Greenspec Clay Tiles, Malta BCA/Greenspec/Cupa Slates, alternative Bitumen Felts).

Expanded Surface-Finishes-And-Boards with specific plaster types (Gypsum Perlite, DBW Generic Gypsum), cement render conditions, alternative lime plaster, alternative plasterboard values (Malta BCA, StdUVal/DBW), and Gypsum Fibreboard.
Added missing Insulated Plasterboard product variants (Siniat GTEC Thermal XP, Unilin Safe-R SR/TB-MF).
Added numerous missing insulation products based on research document.
Added new categories: Other-Insulation-Materials, Concrete-And-Screeds, Roofing-Materials-Outer-Coverings, Surface-Finishes-And-Boards, Insulated-Plasterboard.
Populated new and existing categories with detailed entries for various construction materials (mortars, specific stone types, concrete types, screeds, plasters, renders, roofing layers).
Included specific product lines for insulated plasterboards with various core materials and thicknesses.
Ensured data (lambda, R-value, notes, source) aligned with 'Research_-_Thermal-Properies-Research.txt'.
Added Generic XPS, EPS, Wood-Fibre boards.
Corrected R-value notes for some existing items to specify 100mm where applicable.
- Initial creation of thermal data library
- Added PIR, phenolic, mineral wool, glass mineral wool, masonry and timber materials

Cement-Mortar-Outer-Leaf.source: BR 443:2019 (citing CIBSE Guide A) / Research Doc Sec 3.4

Cement-Mortar-Inner-Leaf.notes: Cement mortar for inner leaf joints (typically 10mm). R-value for 10mm thickness.
Cement-Mortar-Inner-Leaf.info: Standard mortar for internal brick/blockwork. Lower conductivity than outer leaf.
Cement-Mortar-Inner-Leaf.warnings: Mortar joints contribute to thermal bridging in masonry walls.
Cement-Mortar-Inner-Leaf.source: BR 443:2019 (citing CIBSE Guide A) / Research Doc Sec 3.4

Lime-Mortar-1300kg_m3.notes: Lime mortar (Limestone in torba, 1300 kg/m³). R-value for 10mm thickness.
Lime-Mortar-1300kg_m3.info: More breathable mortar, often used in historic building conservation.
Lime-Mortar-1300kg_m3.warnings: Properties can vary based on mix.
Lime-Mortar-1300kg_m3.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 3.4

Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1650kg_m3.notes: Cement mortar (1650 kg/m³). R-value for 10mm thickness.
Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1650kg_m3.warnings: Mortar joints act as thermal bridges.
Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1650kg_m3.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 3.4

Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Dry.notes: Cement mortar (1900 kg/m³, dry). R-value for 10mm thickness.
Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Dry.info: Value from CIBSE Guide A (dry condition).
Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Dry.warnings: Moist condition significantly increases lambda (to 1.5 W/mK).
Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Dry.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 3.4

Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Moist.notes: Cement mortar (1900 kg/m³, moist). R-value for 10mm thickness.
Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Moist.info: Value from CIBSE Guide A (moist condition).
Cement-Mortar-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Moist.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 3.4

Cement-Lime-Plaster-Mortar-CIBSE-1600kg_.notes: Cement/lime plaster (indicative for mortar, 1600 kg/m³). R-value for 10mm thickness.
Cement-Lime-Plaster-Mortar-CIBSE-1600kg_.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 3.4

Mortar-DesigningBuildingsWiki.info: Alternative value from Designing Buildings Wiki.
Mortar-DesigningBuildingsWiki.warnings: Generic value, properties vary with mix.
Mortar-DesigningBuildingsWiki.source: Designing Buildings Wiki / Research Doc Sec 3.4

12.5mm-Thickness.notes: Standard gypsum plasterboard for general internal wall and ceiling applications.
12.5mm-Thickness.info: Complies with EN 520 Type A; suitable for most drylining applications.
12.5mm-Thickness.warnings: Not moisture resistant; avoid use in high humidity areas.

12.5mm-Thickness.notes: Enhanced density plasterboard designed to meet Part E acoustic requirements.
12.5mm-Thickness.info: Mass of 10 kg/m²; reduces sound transmission in residential buildings.
12.5mm-Thickness.warnings: Heavier than standard boards; ensure structural suitability.

12.5mm-Thickness.notes: Fire-resistant plasterboard suitable for areas requiring enhanced fire protection.
12.5mm-Thickness.info: Contains glass fibre and other additives to improve fire performance.
12.5mm-Thickness.warnings: Higher density may affect handling and installation.

12.5mm-Thickness.notes: Moisture-resistant plasterboard for use in areas with intermittent humidity.
12.5mm-Thickness.info: Suitable for kitchens, bathrooms, and utility rooms; complies with EN 520 Type H1.
12.5mm-Thickness.warnings: Not intended for continuous high-humidity environments.

12.5mm-Thickness.notes: High-density plasterboard designed for enhanced acoustic performance.
12.5mm-Thickness.info: Reduces sound transmission; ideal for partitions and separating walls.
12.5mm-Thickness.warnings: Increased weight requires appropriate structural support.

12.5mm-Thickness.notes: Impact-resistant gypsum fibreboard for high-traffic areas.
12.5mm-Thickness.info: Offers superior strength and durability; suitable for schools, hospitals, and public buildings.
12.5mm-Thickness.warnings: Requires appropriate fixings due to increased density.

12.5mm-Thickness.notes: Standard gypsum-based plasterboard for partitions, linings, and ceilings.
12.5mm-Thickness.info: Lightweight and easy to install; suitable for direct decoration or plaster finish.
12.5mm-Thickness.warnings: Not suitable for areas with high moisture exposure.

2mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.notes: Dense gypsum skimming plaster (1200 kg/m³). R-value for 2 mm thickness.
2mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.info: Thin finish coat for internal walls and ceilings.
2mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.warnings: Very thin layer, minimal thermal resistance. Properties vary with mix and application.

3mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.notes: Dense gypsum skimming plaster (1200 kg/m³). R-value for 3 mm thickness.
3mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.info: Standard finish coat for internal walls and ceilings.
3mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.warnings: Very thin layer, minimal thermal resistance. Properties vary with mix and application.

5mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.notes: Dense gypsum skimming plaster (1200 kg/m³). R-value for 5 mm thickness.
5mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.info: Thicker finish coat for internal walls and ceilings where additional smoothing is required.
5mm-Thickness-Skimming-Plaster-Coat.warnings: Thin layer, minimal thermal resistance. Properties vary with mix and application.

10mm-Thickness.notes: General-purpose gypsum-based adhesive for dot-and-dab drylining systems.
10mm-Thickness.info: Suitable for Gyproc DriLyner and other dot-and-dab applications on high, medium or low suction backgrounds; allows finishing same day.
10mm-Thickness.warnings: Ensure substrate is clean, dry and free of dust; follow mixing and application instructions to avoid sagging.
10mm-Thickness.source: British Gypsum Gyproc DriWall Adhesive Product Data Sheet

10mm-Thickness.notes: High-strength gypsum adhesive for plasterboard bonding.
10mm-Thickness.info: Rapid-setting formulation allows dot-and-dab fixing of boards with minimal waiting time before jointing or skimming.
10mm-Thickness.warnings: Mix to manufacturer consistency; use within pot life and protect from frost and extreme heat during cure.

Lightweight-600kg_m3.notes: Lightweight gypsum plaster (600 kg/m³). R-value for 13mm thickness.
Lightweight-600kg_m3.info: Internal wall finish. Better insulator than dense plaster.
Lightweight-600kg_m3.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 7.1

Medium-Density-900kg_m3.notes: Medium density gypsum plaster (900 kg/m³). R-value for 13mm thickness.
Medium-Density-900kg_m3.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 7.1

Dense-1200kg_m3.notes: Dense gypsum plaster (1200 kg/m³). R-value for 13mm thickness.
Dense-1200kg_m3.info: Internal wall finish. More durable, less insulating.
Dense-1200kg_m3.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 7.1

Gypsum-Perlite-Plaster-950kg_m3.notes: Gypsum perlite plaster (950 kg/m³). R-value for 13mm thickness.
Gypsum-Perlite-Plaster-950kg_m3.info: Lightweight plaster with perlite for improved insulation. Same lambda as Malta BCA Lightweight.

Generic-Gypsum-Plaster-DesigningBuilding.notes: Generic gypsum plaster. R-value for 13mm thickness.
Generic-Gypsum-Plaster-DesigningBuilding.info: Alternative generic value from Designing Buildings Wiki. Higher conductivity than other listed gypsum plasters.
Generic-Gypsum-Plaster-DesigningBuilding.source: Designing Buildings Wiki / Research Doc Sec 7.1

External-Render-1300kg_m3.notes: External cement render (1300 kg/m³). R-value for 19mm thickness.
External-Render-1300kg_m3.warnings: Conductivity affected by moisture and density.
External-Render-1300kg_m3.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 7.2

Cement-Plaster-1760kg_m3.notes: Internal cement plaster (1760 kg/m³). R-value for 13mm thickness.
Cement-Plaster-1760kg_m3.info: Durable internal finish, often in wet areas.
Cement-Plaster-1760kg_m3.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 7.2

Rendering-1430kg_m3-1pc-Moisture.notes: Rendering (1430 kg/m³, 1% moisture). R-value for 19mm thickness.
Rendering-1430kg_m3-1pc-Moisture.warnings: Conductivity affected by density and moisture.
Rendering-1430kg_m3-1pc-Moisture.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 7.2

Rendering-1330kg_m3-8pc-Moisture.notes: Rendering (1330 kg/m³, 8% moisture). R-value for 19mm thickness.
Rendering-1330kg_m3-8pc-Moisture.warnings: Higher moisture content increases conductivity compared to very dry mix.
Rendering-1330kg_m3-8pc-Moisture.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 7.2

Sand-Cement-Render-DesigningBuildingsWik.info: Alternative generic value from Designing Buildings Wiki. Close to Malta BCA External Render (0.57 W/mK).
Sand-Cement-Render-DesigningBuildingsWik.source: Designing Buildings Wiki / Research Doc Sec 7.2

Lime-Plaster-Render-1300kg_m3.notes: Lime plaster/render (Limestone in torba, 1300 kg/m³). R-value for 19mm thickness.
Lime-Plaster-Render-1300kg_m3.info: Breathable finish, used in traditional construction.
Lime-Plaster-Render-1300kg_m3.warnings: Properties vary with mix and application.
Lime-Plaster-Render-1300kg_m3.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 7.3

Cement-Lime-Plaster-CIBSE-1600kg_m3.notes: Cement/lime plaster (1600 kg/m³). R-value for 19mm thickness (if render). Same as Malta BCA Lime Plaster/Render.
Cement-Lime-Plaster-CIBSE-1600kg_m3.warnings: Check if for plaster or render thickness.
Cement-Lime-Plaster-CIBSE-1600kg_m3.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 7.3

standard.info: High-density building board with structural, impact, and acoustic properties. Not primarily an insulator.
standard.warnings: Distinct from foam-backed insulated plasterboards.

Insulation-25mm_Overall-37.5mm.info: PIR insulated plasterboard for dry lining applications.

Insulation-40mm_Overall-52.5mm.notes: PIR core (0.022 W/mK) bonded to 12.5mm plasterboard. R-value for composite board.
Insulation-40mm_Overall-52.5mm.info: PIR insulated plasterboard for dry lining applications.

Insulation-50mm_Overall-62.5mm.notes: PIR core (0.022 W/mK) bonded to 12.5mm plasterboard. R-value for composite board.
Insulation-50mm_Overall-62.5mm.info: PIR insulated plasterboard for dry lining applications.

standard.notes: Softwood timber (~500 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.
standard.info: Typically used for structural framing (studs, joists).
standard.warnings: Moisture content affects thermal properties. Acts as thermal bridge in insulated elements.

standard.notes: Hardwood timber (~700 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.
standard.info: Denser wood with higher thermal conductivity than softwood.
standard.warnings: Less commonly used in thermal elements due to higher conductivity and cost.

Reinforced-Concrete-1pc-Steel-2300kg_m3.notes: Reinforced concrete (1% steel, ~2300 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.
Reinforced-Concrete-1pc-Steel-2300kg_m3.info: Common structural concrete. Steel increases conductivity.
Reinforced-Concrete-1pc-Steel-2300kg_m3.warnings: Very poor insulator. Requires significant additional insulation.

Concrete-1800kg_m3-Protected.notes: Concrete (1800 kg/m³, protected/internal). R-value for 100mm thickness.
Concrete-1800kg_m3-Protected.warnings: Thermal performance varies with aggregate and moisture.

Concrete-1800kg_m3-Exposed.notes: Concrete (1800 kg/m³, exposed/external). R-value for 100mm thickness.
Concrete-1800kg_m3-Exposed.warnings: Thermal performance varies with aggregate and moisture.

Concrete-2200kg_m3-Protected.notes: Concrete (2200 kg/m³, protected/internal). R-value for 100mm thickness.

Concrete-2200kg_m3-Exposed.notes: Concrete (2200 kg/m³, exposed/external). R-value for 100mm thickness.

Concrete-2400kg_m3-Protected.notes: Concrete (2400 kg/m³, protected/internal). R-value for 100mm thickness.
Concrete-2400kg_m3-Protected.info: Very dense concrete, lower moisture content.

Concrete-2400kg_m3-Exposed.notes: Concrete (2400 kg/m³, exposed/external). R-value for 100mm thickness.
Concrete-2400kg_m3-Exposed.info: Very dense concrete, higher moisture content.

Cellular-Concrete-400kg_m3.notes: Lightweight cellular concrete (400 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.
Cellular-Concrete-400kg_m3.info: Good thermal performance for concrete due to air voids.
Cellular-Concrete-400kg_m3.warnings: Low compressive strength, not for all structural uses.
Cellular-Concrete-400kg_m3.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 4.1

Cellular-Concrete-1200kg_m3.notes: Cellular concrete (1200 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.
Cellular-Concrete-1200kg_m3.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 4.1

Heavy-Weight-Concrete-2243kg_m3.notes: Heavy weight concrete (2243 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.

Reinforced-Concrete-2pc-Steel-2400kg_m3.notes: Reinforced concrete (2% steel, 2400 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.

Roof-Floor-Slab-Concrete-2000kg_m3.notes: Concrete for roof/floor slab (2000 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.

No-Fines-Concrete-1800kg_m3.notes: No-fines concrete (1800 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.
No-Fines-Concrete-1800kg_m3.info: Concrete with voids, slightly better thermal performance than dense concrete of similar overall density.

Dense-Generic-Concrete-Approx-2300kg_m3.notes: Dense generic concrete (~2300 kg/m³). Lambda range 1.4-1.75 W/mK. R-value for 100mm using mid-range lambda (1.575 W/mK).

Aerated-Generic-Concrete.notes: Aerated generic concrete. R-value for 100mm thickness.
Aerated-Generic-Concrete.info: Better thermal performance due to aeration. Not to be confused with AAC/Cellular.
Aerated-Generic-Concrete.warnings: Distinguish from AAC blocks or cellular concrete which have lower lambdas.

Low-Thermally-Conductive-Concrete-1400kg.notes: Low thermally conductive concrete (1400 kg/m³). Lambda range 0.45-0.8 W/mK. R-value for 100mm using mid-range lambda (0.625 W/mK).
Low-Thermally-Conductive-Concrete-1400kg.info: Specialized concrete with improved thermal properties.

Precast-Hollow-Core-Concrete-Material-12.notes: Precast hollow core concrete (material property, 1290-2105 kg/m³). Lambda range 1.012-1.626 W/mK. R-value for 100mm using mid-range lambda (1.319 W/mK).
Precast-Hollow-Core-Concrete-Material-12.info: Hollow cores improve overall thermal resistance of the element but material lambda is still high.
Precast-Hollow-Core-Concrete-Material-12.warnings: Lambda is for solid material; element U-value calculation needs to account for cores.

Cement-Sand-Screed-BR443.notes: Cement-sand screed (1800 kg/m³). R-value for typical 50mm thickness is 0.043 (BR443 value for 50mm). For 100mm R=0.087.
Cement-Sand-Screed-BR443.info: Common floor screed. Value from BR 443 for 50mm screed.
Cement-Sand-Screed-BR443.warnings: Conductivity varies with mix and density.

Flooring-Roofing-Screed-EN12524.notes: Flooring/roofing screed (1200 kg/m³). R-value for 50mm thickness. For 100mm R=0.244.
Flooring-Roofing-Screed-EN12524.warnings: Confirm density and mix for specific application.
Flooring-Roofing-Screed-EN12524.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 4.2

Anhydrite-Screed-Generic.notes: Calcium sulphate / Anhydrite screed. Lambda typically 1.2-2.0 W/mK. R-value for 50mm at lambda 1.6. For 100mm R=0.063.
Anhydrite-Screed-Generic.info: Often used with underfloor heating due to good conductivity.
Anhydrite-Screed-Generic.warnings: Poor insulator. Lambda varies by product.

Cement-Sand-Screed-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Dry.notes: Cement mortar/screed (1900 kg/m³, dry). R-value for 50mm thickness.
Cement-Sand-Screed-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Dry.info: Value from CIBSE Guide A (cement mortar, indicative for screed).
Cement-Sand-Screed-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Dry.warnings: Conductivity varies with mix, density, and moisture.
Cement-Sand-Screed-CIBSE-1900kg_m3-Dry.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 4.2

standard.notes: Agilia Screed A Gyvlon (Anhydrite, 2000 kg/m³ dry density). Lambda typically 1.2-2.0 W/mK. R-value for 50mm using lambda 1.6 W/mK.
standard.info: Calcium sulphate screed, good for UFH.
standard.warnings: Poor insulator. Confirm lambda from manufacturer.

standard.notes: Concrete roof tiles (2100 kg/m³). R-value for typical 15mm thickness. Negligible in most U-value calcs.
standard.info: Outer weatherproof layer for pitched roofs.
standard.warnings: Thermal resistance usually ignored if roof void is ventilated.
standard.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 6.1 & Table 6.1

standard.notes: Clay roof tiles (1900-2000 kg/m³). Lambda 0.85-1.0. R-value for typical 12mm thickness at lambda 1.0. Negligible in most U-value calcs.
standard.info: Outer weatherproof layer for pitched roofs.
standard.warnings: Thermal resistance usually ignored if roof void is ventilated.
standard.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524, Greenspec / Research Doc Sec 6.2 & Table 6.1

Greenspec-1900kg_m3.notes: Clay roof tiles (1900 kg/m³). R-value for typical 12mm thickness. Negligible in most U-value calcs.
Greenspec-1900kg_m3.info: Alternative value from Greenspec. Differs from Malta BCA (1.0 W/mK).
Greenspec-1900kg_m3.warnings: Thermal resistance usually ignored if roof void is ventilated.

standard.notes: Natural slates for roofing (1600-2800 kg/m³). Lambda 1.0-2.5. R-value for typical 7mm thickness at lambda 2.2. Negligible.
standard.info: Outer weatherproof layer for pitched roofs. Lambda varies significantly.
standard.warnings: Thermal resistance usually ignored if roof void is ventilated.
standard.source: Multiple Sources (Malta BCA, Greenspec, Cupa) / Research Doc Sec 6.3 & Table 6.1

Malta-BCA-13mm-1602kg_m3.notes: Natural slates (13mm thick, 1602 kg/m³). R-value for 13mm thickness. Negligible.
Malta-BCA-13mm-1602kg_m3.info: Specific value from Malta BCA / EN 12524.
Malta-BCA-13mm-1602kg_m3.warnings: Thermal resistance usually ignored if roof void is ventilated.
Malta-BCA-13mm-1602kg_m3.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 6.3 & Table 6.1

Greenspec-2691kg_m3.notes: Natural slates (2691 kg/m³). R-value for typical 7mm thickness. Negligible.
Greenspec-2691kg_m3.info: Alternative value from Greenspec. Very high conductivity.
Greenspec-2691kg_m3.warnings: Thermal resistance usually ignored if roof void is ventilated.

standard.notes: Cupa Pizarras natural slate. R-value for typical 7mm thickness. Negligible.
standard.info: Manufacturer specific value. Higher conductivity parallel to cleavage.
standard.warnings: Thermal resistance usually ignored if roof void is ventilated.
standard.source: Cupa Pizarras / Research Doc Sec 6.3 & Table 6.1

standard.notes: Bituminous roofing felt (1100 kg/m³). Lambda 0.20-0.23. R-value for typical 3mm thickness at lambda 0.23.
standard.info: Waterproofing layer, often in flat roofs or as underlay.
standard.warnings: Usually part of a built-up system. Negligible thermal resistance alone.
standard.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 6.4 & Table 6.1

Felt-On-Flat-Roof-Malta-BCA-1100kg_m3.notes: Bitumen felt on flat roof (1100 kg/m³). R-value for typical 3mm thickness.
Felt-On-Flat-Roof-Malta-BCA-1100kg_m3.info: Alternative value from Malta BCA / EN 12524. Differs from other Malta BCA felt (0.23 W/mK).
Felt-On-Flat-Roof-Malta-BCA-1100kg_m3.source: Malta BCA / EN 12524 / Research Doc Sec 6.4 & Table 6.1

Bitumen-Insulation-Felt-CIBSE-1000kg_m3.notes: Bitumen insulation/felt, all types (1000 kg/m³). R-value for typical 3mm thickness.
Bitumen-Insulation-Felt-CIBSE-1000kg_m3.info: Value from CIBSE Guide A. May refer to bitumen-bonded boards rather than simple felt.
Bitumen-Insulation-Felt-CIBSE-1000kg_m3.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 6.4 & Table 6.1

standard.notes: Cellular glass insulation (140 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm.
standard.info: Rigid, non-combustible, high compressive strength, impervious to water.
standard.warnings: Higher lambda than foam insulations. BS EN 13167.
standard.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 2.7

standard.notes: Wood fibre insulation board (~240 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm.
standard.info: Eco-friendly insulation with good thermal mass and breathability.
standard.warnings: Check suitability for moisture-prone areas. Can be heavier than foam boards.
standard.source: CIBSE Guide A / BS EN 13171 / Research Doc Sec 2.7

standard.notes: Wood fibre board (250-800 kg/m³). Lambda range 0.07-0.18 W/mK. R-value for 100mm thickness using mid-range lambda (0.125 W/mK).
standard.info: Eco-friendly insulation. Properties vary significantly with density.
standard.warnings: Use specific product data due to wide lambda range. Differs from CIBSE value (0.042 W/mK).

standard.notes: Urea Formaldehyde Foam (10 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.
standard.info: Restricted in new builds.
standard.warnings: Check current regulations for use.
standard.source: CIBSE Guide A / Research Doc Sec 2.7

standard.notes: Wood wool slab (500 kg/m³). R-value for 100mm thickness.
standard.info: Cement-bonded wood fibres. Good for acoustics and thermal mass.
standard.warnings: Higher conductivity than dedicated wood fibre insulation boards.
